title: DECODE & SOLVE (ROLE PLAY)
rules:
• Each team will receive a random technology concept.
  • Topics may include AI, Cybersecurity, Cloud Computing, Networking, Digital Safety and Emerging Technologies
  • Teams will receive 20 minutes of preparation time.
  • Phones and internet may be used only during preparation for research.
  • Outside assistance is prohibited.
  • Concepts may be presented through skits, storytelling, roleplay, demonstrations, humour, or analogies.
  • Only simple non-electronic props may be used.
  • The concept must be explained clearly and technically accurately.
  • Content must remain respectful and audience-appropriate.
  • Performance duration: 5 - 8 minutes.
  • A warning bell will ring at 7 minutes; the final bell at 8 minutes.
  • Exceeding 8 minutes may result in a time penalty.
  • The performance should be an act, demonstration, story, analogy, or roleplay.
  • Unfair means or rule violations may lead to penalty or disqualification.
  • The judges and coordinators decision will be final.
  • Chart paper, markers, stationery, and other materials will be provided.
  • Additional instructions will be provided at the venue.

1. Rules and Regulations:
    • Each team must consist of exactly 3 participants. No substitutions or additions will be allowed after the event begins.
    • The competition consists of two rounds:
      • Round 1: Decode
      • Round 2: Solve
    • Final ranking will be based on the total score obtained in Round 1 and Round 2, out of 50 marks.
    • The clues may be based on, but are not limited to Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing, Robotics and Other Emerging Technologies.
  2. Round 1 : Decode
    • Teams must analyze the provided clues and correctly identify the technology, concept, or problem being described.
    • Teams will have 10 minutes to discuss and submit a single answer sheet containing the identified technology or concept.
    • Teams may submit their answer before the allotted time expires. Once submitted, no changes or resubmissions will be permitted.
    • During this round, the use of mobile phones, smartwatches, laptops, tablets, calculators, internet access, AI tools, or any other electronic device is strictly prohibited.
    • Only teams that correctly identify the intended technology/concept in Round 1 will proceed to Round 2. The judges' interpretation of the clues and their scoring decisions shall be final.
  3. Round 2: Solve
    • The teams will design a solution (system, app, workflow, architecture or prototype concept) to a real-world problem.
    • Teams will have 10 minutes to prepare using the chart paper / materials provided. Output maybe an architecture diagram, flowchart, algorithm, pseudocode, interface sketch or verbal proposal.
    • Round 2 presentation time shall be a maximum of 7 minutes, followed by up to 3 minutes for judges questions. The judges may stop a team when the allotted presentation time expires.
    • The proposed solution must clearly explain:
      • How the technology works
      • How it solves the given problem
      • Why the solution is practical and technically feasible
    • The teams will be judged on technical understanding, logical reasoning, creativity, and feasibility.
    • All three team members must present and make take any question. Judges may also ask for an individual response.
    • If two or more teams are tied on total score, judges will ask the tied teams extra questions in a tie-breaker round to decide the final rank.
judging:
Round 1

  • Interpretation and Analysis of the clues [10 Points]
  • Identification of the technology/ Concept [5 Points]

Total: 15

Round 2

  • Understanding the Problem [7 Points]
  • Technical Solution [8 Points]
  • Innovation and Creativity [7 Points]
  • Presentation and Communication [7 Points]
  • Technical Questions [6 Points]

Total: 35
